caption: The environment of the agent: the variable-density solver of the package on the Henry benchmark of seawater intrusion (Henry number 0.1). (a) Relative salinity and the 0.5 isochlor on a 61 × 31 grid; its toe lies 1.386 m from the inland boundary. (b) The toe converges as the mesh is refined (1.423, 1.397, 1.392 and 1.386 m), with Newton residuals below 10⁻¹².

The certified alarm whose margins the shield uses, on a synthetic chloride record: a forecast, a margin of 23.9 mg/L calibrated on 600 earlier steps, and the alarm level of 226.1 mg/L. (a) In the 600 live steps all 23 events at or above 250 mg/L were warned (none missed; 95% upper bound on the miss rate 0.122). (b) The calibration errors and the margin.

Warnings between samples. (a) The probability that chloride crosses 250 mg/L within a season of 120 days depends on its correlation time: 0.79 at 8 days, while the samples alone give 0.023. (b) The robust warning band from an 8-year record narrows from quarterly samples (0.18–1.00) to monthly (0.44–1.00), weekly (0.78–0.89) and a daily logger (0.79–0.82).

The learned boundary of Part 5 in the environment: a 2-km model of a 10-km aquifer predicts ten years of drought with doubled pumping. (a) With the boundary learned from two piezometers the head at the boundary cell stays within 0.0049 m (rms) of the whole aquifer, against 0.605 m with no flow and 1.234 m with a fixed head. (b) The impedance of the learned boundary matches the exact exterior within 1% at periods of one to forty years.

The network that observes the environment. (a) Among 12 candidate salinity sensors, the greedy design [4, 7, 8] for the salt mass near the toe equals the exhaustive optimum (2.539 nats) and gives 100% of the best information on whether the supply cell exceeds its limit. (b) The gain after each added sensor, against all 220 designs of three sensors (median 1.457 nats).

The forcing of the environment read from the heads. (a) Daily recharge reconstructed from heads with 1 cm noise (rms error 2.8 mm, as predicted). (b) Sums over 30 days: rms error 2.6 mm against a mean of 32.4 mm. The heads give the timing of the recharge and, with the specific yield from a pumping test, its amount.
